title: The Middle Voice
subtitle: Action for or upon oneself — λύομαι.
objectives: Conjugate any regular ω-verb in the present indicative middle.
Understand the middle voice as action for or upon oneself.
Distinguish middle from active in meaning and form.

sections.heading: The middle voice
sections.body:
Greek has three voices: active, middle, and passive. The active voice is action done by the subject to an object. The middle voice is action done by the subject for or upon itself. The passive voice is action done to the subject by an agent (you will learn this in the next lesson).

λύω — I loose (active: I loose something else)
λύομαι — I loose for myself, I free myself (middle: I loose something for my own benefit or I loose myself)

The middle voice is hard to translate into English because English has no middle voice. Greek uses the middle when the subject has a personal stake in the action or when the action affects the subject directly.

sections.heading: The present indicative middle: λύομαι
sections.body:
singular
  1st   λύομαι      I loose for myself
  2nd   λύῃ         you loose for yourself
  3rd   λύεται      he/she/it looses for himself/herself/itself

  plural
  1st   λυόμεθα     we loose for ourselves
  2nd   λύεσθε      you (plural) loose for yourselves
  3rd   λύονται     they loose for themselves

The endings are -μαι, -σαι (contracts to -ῃ), -ται, -μεθα, -σθε, -νται. The thematic vowel is still ο/ε, as in the active.

sections.heading: Examples of the middle voice
sections.body:
παύομαι — I stop (myself), I cease (middle of παύω, I stop something else)

πείθομαι — I obey, I trust (middle of πείθω, I persuade). The middle means 'I persuade myself' = 'I am persuaded' = 'I trust'.

γράφομαι — I write for myself, I have written (middle of γράφω). In practice, this might mean 'I commission a writing' or 'I record for my own use'.

The middle voice is common in Greek. Many verbs prefer the middle when the subject is involved in the result of the action.

sections.heading: From Xenophon
sections.body:
Anabasis I.3.1: ἐντεῦθεν ἐξελαύνει.
'From there he marches forth.' ἐξελαύνει is active. If it were middle (ἐξελαύνεται), it might mean 'he marches forth for himself' or 'he rides out' (emphasizing his personal involvement).

What is the basic meaning of the middle voice?
items.answer: Action for or upon oneself — the subject has a personal stake in the action.

words.gloss: I free myself from the chains.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.2 introduces the passive voice. In the present and imperfect tenses, the passive is identical in form to the middle. Context distinguishes. λύομαι can mean 'I free myself' (middle) or 'I am freed' (passive).

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can conjugate the present middle of any ω-verb from memory and can distinguish middle from active in meaning.
